scenario: Two friends are hanging out at home and deciding what music to listen to
learner_goal: Listen to your favorite band (<extra_info>Extra information: your favorite band just released a new album</extra_info>)
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Samuel stays true to his background as a software developer and cook, offering snacks and coffee while negotiating a compromise that honors both his goal and his friend's needs.
[relationship] Samuel shows empathy for Oliver's stressful day and proposes a fair compromise, strengthening the friendship.
[knowledge] Samuel learns that Oliver had a stressful day and prefers classical music (specifically Debussy or Mozart) to relax.
[secret] Samuel did not reveal his past as a figure skater.
[social_rules] Samuel followed social norms for hosting and friendship.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No material gains or losses occurred.
[goal] Samuel secured a firm agreement to play his favorite band's new album immediately following a 30-minute relaxation period.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Oliver's request for calming music aligns perfectly with his stressful day as a police officer.
[relationship] Oliver is appreciative of Samuel's flexibility and hospitality, reinforcing their mutual respect.
[knowledge] Oliver learns that Samuel's favorite band has a new album and that Samuel is willing to accommodate his mood.
[secret] Oliver did not reveal his greenhouse or love for gardening.
[social_rules] Oliver communicated his needs politely and accepted a compromise.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No material gains or losses occurred.
[goal] Oliver successfully negotiated for the peaceful classical music he needed to relax after a stressful day.

transcript.speaker: Samuel Anderson
transcript.content: said: "Hey Oliver — my favorite band just released a new album. Want to give it a spin? I can make coffee and whip up some snacks while we listen."

transcript.speaker: Oliver Smith
transcript.content: Cheers, Sam — that sounds great, but I’ve had a rough day and was hoping for something calming. Mind if we put on some peaceful classical instead, maybe Debussy or a gentle Mozart piano concerto? Coffee and snacks would still be perfect though.

transcript.speaker: Samuel Anderson
transcript.content: Totally get it — rough days cry out for something soothing. How about this: I’ll make coffee and snacks and put on Debussy for, say, 30 minutes while you unwind, then we switch to my band’s new album? Or if you’d prefer, I can play the new record quietly in the background now — it’s got some mellow tracks. Which would you rather do?

transcript.speaker: Oliver Smith
transcript.content: Perfect, Sam — Debussy for 30 minutes sounds ideal. Thanks, I could really use that; coffee and snacks would be great, and then we can cue up your album afterward.
